newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat will go to Washington, PLO official says.
newsitem.headline: Arafat will go to Washington, PLO official says.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will go to Washington, where U.S. President Bill Clinton is hosting a Middle East summit, after talks in Luxembourg with European ministers, a Palestinian official said on Monday.
"He is going now to Luxembourg and then Washington," said the official, who declined to be named.
Clinton on Sunday invited Arafat to a Middle East summit with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday but Arafat asked him to postpone it.

Arafat and his main Arab ally, Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, want to be sure the summit will produce firm guarantees that Netanyahu will carry out agreements the previous government signed with the Palestinians.
The United States has not responded in public to Arafat's request for a postponement, saying only that he accepted the invitation on Sunday and they expected him to come.
Arafat had more than two hours of talks with Mubarak at Burg al-Arab near the Egyptian city of Alexandria on Monday and then flew to Cairo for a flight to Europe.
On arrival in Cairo, he told reporters: "I received an invitation from...President Clinton and I sent him my reply."
Asked what his reply was, he said: "I can't say before he receives the reply...The important thing is how to implement accurately what has been agreed upon (with Israel)."
The Palestinian official gave no further details. He did not say if the United States or Israel had done anything to persuade Arafat to change his mind.
Egypt did not make clear Mubarak's plans but security officials said the Egyptian president was expected to arrive in Cairo shortly from Alexandria.
